title: Fetch every page of the report on a pool

blocks.text: The billing service downloads a paginated invoice report by running one task per page on a thread pool, then putting the pages back in order. Pages are numbered from 1.
Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/PageFetcher.java`: `tasks(pageCount)` builds the tasks that `fetchAll` hands to the pool. The pool runs them after `tasks` has returned, in any order.
When you're done, a report of four pages comes back as pages 1, 2, 3 and 4, each fetched once. About four lines in total.

cases.says: there is one task for each page of the report, and none for an empty one
each task, run on the pool after the tasks are built, fetches its own page, so every page arrives once and in order

origin.section: A Lambda Can Capture the Enhanced for's Variable, Not the Basic for's Counter

concepts: A lambda can't capture a basic for's counter, which the update changes; a variable declared in the body, or the enhanced for's variable, is new each pass and can be captured.
